topicName: Evaluation Metrics for Classification and Regression
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Evaluation Metrics for Classification and Regression"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Selecting the right evaluation metric is crucial for determining how well a machine learning model generalizes to unseen data. Different problems require different metrics, and relying on the wrong one can lead to severely flawed models."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Classification Metrics"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Classification problems involve predicting discrete class labels. The choice of metric depends heavily on class distribution and the business cost of false positives versus false negatives."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Accuracy: The ratio of correct predictions to total predictions. Can be misleading in imbalanced datasets."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Precision and Recall: Precision measures exactness (True Positives / (True Positives + False Positives)), while Recall measures completeness (True Positives / (True Positives + False Negatives))."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"F1-Score: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a single score for balancing both concerns."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ROC-AUC: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve, measuring the model\'s ability to discriminate between classes across various threshold settings."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Regression Metrics"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Regression problems involve predicting continuous numerical values. Metrics here quantify the magnitude of errors made by the model."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mean Absolute Error (MAE): The average of absolute differences between predictions and actual values. Less sensitive to outliers."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mean Squared Error (MSE): The average of squared differences. Heavily penalizes large errors due to the squaring operation."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE): The square root of MSE, bringing the error metric back to the original scale of the target variable."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"R-Squared (Coefficient of Determination): Represents the proportion of variance in the dependent variable that is predictable from the independent variables."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Python Implementation Example"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Here is a quick Python snippet using Scikit-Learn to calculate both classification and regression metrics."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score, mean_squared_error, r2_score

# Classification Example
y_true_clf = [0, 1, 1, 0, 1]
y_pred_clf = [0, 1, 0, 0, 1]
acc = accuracy_score(y_true_clf, y_pred_clf)
f1 = f1_score(y_true_clf, y_pred_clf)
print(f\'Accuracy: {acc}, F1: {f1}\')

# Regression Example
y_true_reg = [2.5, 0.0, 2.1, 8.0]
y_pred_reg = [3.0, -0.5, 2.0, 7.0]
mse = mean_squared_error(y_true_reg, y_pred_reg)
r2 = r2_score(y_true_reg, y_pred_reg)
print(f\'MSE: {mse}, R2: {r2}\')"}]
